REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1, u2
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u2
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, blue_key_picked_up & blue_pyramid_made) -> u1
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, blue_pyramid_on_right) -> u2
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, else) -> u2
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, blue_key_picked_up & blue_pyramid_made, u1) -> 0.1
(u1, blue_pyramid_on_right, u2) -> 1.0
feedback: Accepted. (1) Semantic fidelity: the task is a two-stage ordered property — pick up the blue key (which per the ruleset fires the holding rule on the same step, so `blue_key_picked_up` and `blue_pyramid_made` co-occur) and only then fire the goal. The u0->u1 transition labeled with the conjunction `blue_key_picked_up & blue_pyramid_made` fires exactly on that single co-occurrence step, and u1->u2 on `blue_pyramid_on_right` enforces the required order; the goal cannot fire before the make (environment constraint), so no u0 goal transition is needed and none is rewarded. (2) Event/persistent distinction: all three propositions are events, and every transition reads them as single-step events — no persistence is assumed (e.g., the RM correctly does not treat `blue_pyramid_on_right` as a persistent state of the world). (3) Reachability: u0->u1 is reachable (blue key is initially in the world, pickup with empty pocket), u1->u2 is reachable (putdown while facing map-east so the pyramid lands on the right cell, or forward with the pyramid placed on the right cell); the made pyramid cannot be destroyed, so no regression transitions are required, and none are claimed. (4) Totality/irrelevant events: every state has an else self-loop (u0, u1, u2), so turns, toggles, blocked moves, failed pickups, and any other irrelevant steps are covered without state change or reward. (5) Reward safety/density: rewards only on progressing edges (0.1 for the make/pickup step, 1.0 for the goal step), zero on self-loops; the 0.1 shaping is bounded and is the densest possible given the predicate set (the pickup is the only intermediate event); max total 1.1. (6) Format: REWARD_MACHINE with STATES, INITIAL_STATE, nonempty FINAL_STATES (u2, declared in STATES and accepting — reached exactly on the goal step, which terminates the episode), a deterministic total TRANSITION_FUNCTION, and a REWARD_FUNCTION keyed to transitioning edges only. Compact at three states, matching the two-stage task.

All three declared propositions are implemented and the function set matches the environment's proposition set exactly, with no extras and no omissions. blue_pyramid_made checks membership in env.products_made, correctly reading the event from the rules that fired on the last step rather than the grid, so it is true only on the step a rule made a blue pyramid and false otherwise, including while the tile remains in the world. blue_key_picked_up compares env.picked_up to "blue key", which per the documented API reports the tile the last step's pickup took from the grid (the holding rule may have transformed it in the pocket afterwards, but picked_up preserves the original name), correctly capturing the pickup event and matching the note that it fires on the same step as the rule. blue_pyramid_on_right reads env.goal_reached, the documented flag that is true only on the goal-firing step. All three are event propositions and the code correctly reads them from last-step records instead of inspecting the grid or treating them as persistent state. All returns are genuine booleans, the Python is syntactically valid and executable, and there are no imports, actions, side effects, or mutations of the environment or episode memory; the previous valuation is neither read nor written, which is appropriate since these events are directly observable from the last-step API. The documented API surface (env.products_made, env.picked_up, env.goal_reached) is used within its stated scope.
